chart.title: {market}, {tf}, {bars} candles
chart.fallback: Live candles could not be loaded ({reason}). Showing sample data instead.
chart.source.spot: Spot prices from Binance, times in UTC. Your broker's prices will differ.
chart.source.futures: Prices of a Binance perpetual contract that follows this market, times in UTC. Your broker's prices, hours and spread will differ.
chart.source.custom: Your file, read in this browser and sent nowhere. Its times are taken as UTC.

stats.title: Backtest
stats.holdoutNote: Figures of the first {first}% of the candles. The last {last}% is held back.
stats.size.equity: {n}% of the balance in each trade
stats.size.risk: {n}% of the balance risked per trade
stats.assumptions: Simulated on a 10,000 account, {size}, and {cost}% of cost per side ({fee}% commission plus {slip}% slippage). Past data, not a forecast.
stats.few: Few trades ({n}): not enough to tell skill from luck. Load more candles, try a lower timeframe or loosen the conditions.
stats.none: No trades on these candles: the entry condition never happened.
stats.indicatorOnly: Add a Buy or Sell block to turn this into a strategy and see how it would have traded.
stats.error: The engine could not run this strategy: {msg}
rob.holdout: Hold back the last {last}% of the candles (out-of-sample test)
rob.holdoutHint: Tick it before you start tuning: the trades and figures of that last part stay hidden. When the strategy is finished, untick it and see how it does on candles it never saw. It only counts the first time.
rob.verdict.few: Too few trades in one of the two parts to compare them.
rob.verdict.both: It makes money in both parts. That is what an idea with an edge looks like, though it guarantees nothing.
rob.verdict.faded: It makes money in the first part and gives it back in the last. Common in strategies fitted to old data.
rob.verdict.late: It only makes money in the last part. Check whether that is the strategy or just the market going up.
rob.verdict.neither: It loses money in both parts.
rob.mc: The same {n} trades, drawn at random 1,000 times (Monte Carlo)
rob.mc.p5: With bad luck (5 in 100 end worse)
rob.mc.dd: Drawdown to be ready for (1 in 20)
rob.mc.few: The luck test (Monte Carlo) needs at least {n} closed trades.
rob.mcHint: Your backtest is one path through those trades. If the bad-luck row is deep in the red, the result leaned on the order they happened to come in.
settings.title: Trade management
settings.trailHint: The stop follows the best price at this distance and never moves back.
settings.beHint: Once the trade is this far in profit, the stop moves to the entry price.
settings.maxBars: Close after this many bars (0 = never)
settings.size: Size of each trade in the backtest
settings.sizeHint.equity: Each trade uses this share of the balance.
settings.sizeHint.risk: Each trade is sized so that hitting the stop costs this share of the balance (never more than 20 times the balance). It needs a stop. The lot in the alert is still the fixed one below.
settings.symbolHint: Fill it in only if your broker names it differently (XAUUSD.m, GOLD...).
settings.accountHint: MT5 account: fill it in to send the orders to one account only, with its MT5 login number or the name you gave it in SignalForge. Left empty, every MT5 account you have connected receives them. If it matches no connected account, the order is not placed.
warn.needsNumber: A condition is connected where a number is expected. It was ignored.
warn.logicNeedsTwo: An AND/OR block needs two conditions connected. It was left out.
warn.notNeedsOne: A NOT block has no condition connected. It was left out.
warn.actionNeedsCondition: An order block has no condition connected, so it would never fire. It was left out.
warn.rrNeedsStop: A target measured in stops needs a stop. Pick a stop or another kind of target.
warn.beNeedsStop: A break-even measured in stops needs a stop. Pick a stop or another kind of break-even.
warn.riskNeedsStop: Sizing by risk needs a stop: without one there is no telling how much a trade can lose. The whole balance is used instead.
warn.htfEmpty: {block} ({length}, {tf}) gives no value on this data: its first one comes after {first} finished candles of that timeframe and the candles loaded hold {have}. Whatever is wired to it never fires. Load more candles, or use a shorter length or a lower timeframe.
warn.htfShort: {block} ({length}, {tf}) has little history here: {have} candles of that timeframe, and it takes about {need} for the point where the data starts to stop weighing on it. TradingView loads another amount of history, so its value there will not be the same. Load more candles, or use a shorter length or a lower timeframe.
error.loop: Two blocks feed each other in a circle. Remove one of the connections.
error.empty: Nothing to build yet. Connect a condition to an order, or draw something on the chart.

mt5.title: Send it to MT5
mt5.intro: The script already carries the message SignalForge needs. Four steps:
mt5.step1: Copy the script, open the Pine Editor in TradingView, paste it and press Add to chart.
mt5.step2: Create an alert. Condition: this strategy. If TradingView asks what should trigger it, choose Order fills only.
mt5.step4: Tick Webhook URL and paste the webhook from your SignalForge dashboard.
mt5.sample: What MT5 receives on a buy:
mt5.lotNote: SignalForge trades the lot in the message only when Position size is set to From the signal for that account. With Fixed lot or % risk, the size set in SignalForge is the one traded.
mt5.note: TradingView only sends webhooks on its paid plans.
mt5.needStrategy: Add a Buy or Sell block first: without orders there is nothing to send.
mt5.stopNote: The stop, the target, the trailing and the break-even live in TradingView, not at your broker: when one is hit, TradingView sends the close.
